title: Curvature identification with an invalid finite-valued instrument
description: Develop a source-assisted known-result statistical analysis, not a novel causal claim. Let observations (Z,D,Y) be iid, with Z uniform on {-2,-1,0,1,2}, D=c Z+a Z^2+delta, and Y=beta D+b0+gamma Z+epsilon. The disturbances have conditional means zero given Z, finite fourth moments, and may be correlated with each other. The distribution of Z and the violation space span{1,Z} are known; c,a,beta,b0,gamma are unknown. Establish when beta is identified from the conditional means of D and Y under these restrictions. Work in L2 of the specified instrument law: derive the residual of Z^2 after population projection onto span{1,Z}, then derive identification, the corresponding ratio-of-sample-moments estimator, its asymptotic linear representation, and a heteroskedasticity-robust asymptotic standard error under strong identification. Give an observational-equivalence argument for the a=0 boundary. Keep identification, consistency, asymptotic approximation and finite-sample behavior distinct. Use reviewable Markdown/LaTeX with explicit assumptions and equation-by-equation justification. Implement the empirical moment-ratio procedure using the population residual under the known Z law, not sample residualization or an oracle value of a. The public run_estimator ABI takes equally long arrays z,d,y and returns status, beta, standard_error, n and moment_denominator. When the empirical identifying denominator is exactly zero, report status='zero_moment' with null beta and standard_error; this numerical event is not a statistical test of population identification. For other valid inputs return status='ok', the empirical ratio, the plug-in standard error from the empirical second moment of its estimating-function residual, n and the empirical denominator. Investigate the theory and source with useful exploratory calculations of your choice. Then run fresh fixed-count confirmation for two independent Gaussian-disturbance scenarios, each with n=600, c=1, b0=0, Var(delta)=Var(epsilon)=1: scenario 'positive_curvature' has a=0.5,beta=2,gamma=0.75,Corr(delta,epsilon)=0.6; scenario 'negative_curvature' has a=-0.75,beta=-1,gamma=0.5,Corr(delta,epsilon)=-0.4. Choose at least 1000 datasets per scenario and report all attempted datasets, numerical failures, estimate and standard-error vectors, bias with its Monte Carlo standard error, nominal 95 percent Wald interval coverage and its Monte Carlo standard error. Target coverage MCSE<=0.01; freeze the future count and your scientific criteria before confirmation. The simulation metrics contain scenarios, an array with each scenario_id,a,beta_true,n,n_replicates,estimates,standard_errors,failed_replicates,mean_error,bias_mcse,coverage,coverage_mcse. Null entries in paired vectors retain failed slots rather than dropping them. Each scenario uses the same declared future replicate count; the executable simulation ABI additionally returns acceptance_passed and requested_runtime_replicates. Explore a=0 separately without interpreting arbitrary finite ratios or apparently narrow intervals as valid inference. Obtain independent review and return exact selected theory, implementation, confirmation and unresolved gaps. This finite-law specialization investigates the projection principle in Section 2 of Carl, Emmenegger, Guo and Bühlmann, TSCI: Causal Inference with Invalid Instruments in R, Journal of Statistical Software 114(7), 2025, DOI 10.18637/jss.v114.i07, https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v114i07. It is not the full TSCI estimator, adaptive violation selection, author-code replication, historical rediscovery or a claim that arbitrary invalid instruments identify effects. The frozen local paper text is available through the source tools; author code, reference outputs and hidden numerical checks are not supplied. Formalization is not requested.
